Example course · Dangerous goods

ADR training

Example course for drivers who carry dangerous goods by road.

Enquire about ADRCall 01632 960214

Example course on this demonstration. It is not a booking for a real centre.

In plain English

ADR is the training associated with the carriage of dangerous goods by road. This page is an example course. It does not name classes, tanks or packages, and it does not claim an approval number.

Who it is for

Drivers who need ADR training for the work they do. Whether that is an initial course or a refresher, and which classes apply, is confirmed when you enquire.

What it covers

  • Training towards carrying dangerous goods by road, in the form the course actually covers

Classes, packages and tanks are not listed, because none are specified on this example course.

Eligibility and prerequisites

General guidance, not a check of your licence.

  • A driving entitlement suited to the vehicle being used
  • A note of which ADR classes are needed. None are stated here
  • This example page does not confirm that a particular driver needs ADR

What the training includes

  • Who the course is for
  • Whether it is initial training or a refresher, confirmed when you enquire
  • The classes covered, named only when they are real
  • The example base that lists the course

How the course works

  1. Enquire about ADR

    Say what you carry, or that you are not sure which class applies.

  2. Confirm the course type

    Initial or refresher, packages or tanks, and the classes. None of those are fixed on this example page.

  3. Attend the course

    Classroom training, with a practical element only where the real course includes one.

  4. Ask about the certificate

    How a certificate is issued is explained when you enquire. No approval is claimed here.

Training format

Example classroom course at the base that lists ADR. No syllabus code is published.

Duration and cost

How long the training takes is confirmed when you enquire.

Ask for a quote. No fee or date is listed on this page.

Why train here

  • The course, stated plainly

    Who it is for, what it leads to, and how the training runs, before anyone is asked to commit.

  • Courses matched to a base

    Each course lists the example bases that run it. A base does not advertise training it does not offer.

  • Practical and classroom routes

    Licence training is time in the vehicle. Driver CPC, ADR and Operator CPC are set out as their own courses.

  • A straight enquiry

    The form asks for a course, a preferred base and how you would like to be contacted. It does not book a test.
